title: Adding — putting together

parent.learn: Adding means putting groups together to find how many in all.
parent.why: 2 apples and 1 more apple, pushed together, is one group of 3. The sign + just means “put together”.

parent.learn: Count on from the bigger number.
parent.why: For 2 + 7, start at 7 and say “8, 9”. It is quicker than counting all nine from 1, and gives the same answer.
It is the same things, just moved around, so the total cannot change. This lets you always start with the bigger number.
Ten is the base of our numbers. For 9 + 3, move 1 from the 3 to make 10, then 2 more is 12.
Putting “nothing” with a group leaves it the same size.

ask: You have 3 toy cars. I give you 2 more. How many now?
Show 4 fingers on one hand and 3 on the other — how many in all?
2 people at the table and 3 more come. How many plates do we need?
What is 5 + 5? Use your two hands.
If I give you 0 sweets, how many more do you have?
7 + something makes 10 — what is the something?
Make up your own adding story with your toys.

rounds.h: Start at 2 and count on 1 more.
Start at 2 and count on 2 more.
Start at 3 and count on 2 more.
Start at 1 and count on 1 more.
Adding nothing keeps it the same: 4.
Start at 5 and count on 3 more.
Start at 6 and count on 4 more.

rounds.t: Ravi has 4 balls. He gets 2 more. How many balls now?

rounds.h: Swapping the order gives the same total, so 3 + 5 = 5 + 3.
10 and 5 more: 1 ten and 5 ones is 15.
Make ten first: 9 + 1 = 10, then 2 more is 12.
Make ten first: 8 + 2 = 10, then 4 more is 14.

rounds.t: 12 children are in class. 5 more come in. How many now?
